message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.58,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked or scored vote fairly compares the three distinct allocations and avoids assuming that equal funding is automatically equitable; fairness improves if demand, access, and lifecycle costs are made transparent.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Favors expanding the youth book collection, prioritizing traditional educational and recreational resources.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Favors creating a free-access digital space, emphasizing Internet and technology access, though recurring costs require scrutiny.","influence":0.34},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Favors splitting the subsidy equally between books and digital access as a balanced compromise, but the equal split may not match actual needs or costs.","influence":0.33}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"The three options reflect legitimate but competing service priorities, with no decisive evidence that one universally dominates. Use a transparent social-choice process, ideally ranked or score voting informed by demand and total-cost estimates, then seek a conditional compromise such as phased funding, a pilot digital space, or an adaptive allocation rather than an arbitrary 50/50 split."}
